# A run that waits in recv shows the step that waits, the topic and the deadline, in the text and in the JSON. A message ends the wait and the status loses it.
isolate

exec git init -q -b main origin
exec git -C origin add readme.txt
exec git -C origin -c user.name=e2e -c user.email=e2e@example.com commit -q -m start

subst config/projects/local.star

exec beehestreal item add local ship-it --title 'Ship it' --body-file body.txt
exec beehestreal run ship-it local --workflow flow/recv.star &
waitstatus 'waits for a message on topic findings'

# The run waits in recv, with a 48 hour deadline. It names the call, not the record of its deadline.
exec beehestreal status
stdout 'now recv:findings#1\s'
stdout 'waits for a message on topic findings until [0-9TZ:-]+, 1d23h left'
! stdout 'deadline'

exec beehestreal status --json
stdout '"now":"recv:findings#1"'
stdout '"receiving":"findings"'
stdout '"deadline":"'
stdout '"time_left_seconds":'

exec beehestreal send ship-it --topic findings 'all fine'
wait

exec beehestreal status
stdout 'done'
! stdout 'waits for a message'
exec beehestreal status --json
stdout '"state":"done"'
! stdout '"receiving"'

-- origin/readme.txt --
The source repository.
-- body.txt --
Ship it.
-- config/projects/local.star --
project(
    source      = "@WORK@/origin",
    base_branch = "main",
    gate        = "true",
    test_report = "r.xml",
)
-- flow/recv.star --
def main(item):
    recv("findings", timeout = "48h", name = "findings")
